module_api.entry: render(data, ctx) -> {'html', 'title', 'kicker', 'nav_label', 'css', 'js', 'problems'}. A structural error (shape, type, reference) gives {'html': '', 'problems': [...]}: nothing is drawn. A reader finding (the reader rules in a text, an unknown key, a question id the page does not have) is returned in problems with the html: the build fails, and a draft (audit/rejected.html) still draws the atlas from the fields it knows
module_api.called_by: foundation status.Build.atlas(): loads atlas.py by path, passes json of folder/atlas.json and AtlasContext(self), after every other section is built; wraps html in <section id=atlas class='section wide atlas' data-atlas-mount>
ctx_used: rich(text, terms): glossary buttons on (TERMS = True) in statements, hypotheses and plain text, never inside a link; the two formula box classes are renamed atlas-math-display and atlas-math-long
ident(question id) and anchors: a question id links to '#q-' + ident(id) only when that anchor is in ctx.anchors
anchors (an atlas id already on the page, or used twice by the atlas, is a problem)
labels (page.json: 'atlas', 'atlas_kicker', 'nav_atlas' and any 'atlas_<key>' replace the interface words; every word is checked with the reader rules)
mark(legacy code): the key shows the page's mark for the page status of each atlas status (PAGE_STATUS, the status-language ruling)
ctx_not_used: mark for the atlas's own statuses (the atlas draws its squares)
module_api.also_reads: audit.FORBIDDEN (module constant, read only) to check every string and id before rendering
module_api.assets: css = atlas.css (placed by foundation after status.css, before status-print.css); js = atlas.js (its own <script> after status.js); neither contains </script>, url() other than #fragment, a network call, a file name or a page forbidden word

data.schema: programme-scientific-atlas-public/v1: top level schema, domains, claims, edges, comparisons, readingPaths, optional asOf (read, never shown). Optional fields: domains[].conventions, domains[].relatedQuestionIds, claims[].sourceLabel, claims[].comparisonIds, claims[].statementRef, comparisons[].questionId, comparisons[].relatedQuestionIds, readingPaths[].note
data.unknown_keys: a reader finding at every level: the build fails and names it; nothing of it is shown
rules: ids: ^[a-z0-9]+([_-][a-z0-9]+)*$, at most 64, unique per kind, no hash-like run of 7+ hex characters; ids are never shown as text
every shown string, and every id read with _ and - as spaces: audit.FORBIDDEN; no address of another host, no percentage, no LaTeX label (thm:, prop:, lem:, eq:, ...)
a conditional claim lists at least one hypothesis, and a scoped negative claim the hypotheses of its scope (reader findings)
edges: existing endpoints, no self edge, no duplicate (source, target, relation); a relation code is words joined by _, - or spaces; each edge keeps its own label, which reads from source to target
relation types: any number; up to 8 have their own line style; with more, every line is plain and the key says so (each relation is named in both claims' lists)

comparisons: each listed claim's code matches its list; a claim in one list at most; at least one claim; claim.comparisonIds (optional) must equal the comparisons that list the claim; questionId and relatedQuestionIds (optional) must name questions of the page
domains: conventions (optional) a list of non-empty strings; relatedQuestionIds (optional) must name questions of the page

readingPaths: kind editorial_orientation (any stages) or source_bound_dependency_path (two or more stages, each with a claim, every claim of the first stage joined to the second and every later claim joined to the stage before by a recorded edge in either direction); note (optional) shown under the summary
statementRef (optional): ctx.anchor_for(id) must give the anchor of a statement on the page

status.code in checked|conditional|scoped_negative|remaining; the visible word is chosen by the code (Established, Conditional, Remaining, Scoped negative); status.label is a display alias, kept and checked but not shown
never_derived: no count, ratio, percentage or progress cue
no status beyond the supplied code and label
no dependency or proof wording for a path: a path of the second kind is labelled 'Joined by recorded relations' because that is what is checked

quality_mapping.nodes: [data-claim-id] with data-status-: article.atlas-claim#atlas-c-<id>[data-claim-id=<id>][data-status-code=<code>][data-domain-id]; visible: chip with the group name and 'Status: <supplied label>'
quality_mapping.edges: [data-edge-id][data-source][data-: on every rendered relation: li.atlas-rel in the source's ul[data-dir=out] and in the target's ul[data-dir=in], path.atlas-edge in the map, path.atlas-hood-edge in the pane diagram (script), li in a path's join list
quality_mapping.paths: [data-path-id][data-path-kind]: article.atlas-path#atlas-p-<id>[data-path-id][data-path-kind]; editorial ones labelled 'Editorial order' in visible text
quality_mapping.text equivalent: every relation is a sentence in both claims' lists; the map and the diagram are aria-hidden drawings whose marks are tabindex=-1 links
quality_mapping.data: fully recoverable from the DOM attributes; no embedded JSON

dom_hooks.references_not_claims: index rows tr#atlas-r-<id>[data-claim-ref], map and diagram marks a.atlas-node[data-claim-ref], map domain names a.atlas-track, domain cards article#atlas-d-<id>[data-domain-id], comparisons article#atlas-k-<id>[data-comparison-id], key items [data-key-status] and [data-key-relation][data-key-style], question links a.atlas-question-link[data-question-ref]
dom_hooks.anchors: parts: atlas-overview (map and key), atlas-domains, atlas-claims (index), atlas-comparisons, atlas-paths, atlas-full; items: atlas-d-, atlas-c-, atlas-k-, atlas-p-, atlas-r-; headings of items: <item id>--h (ids cannot contain --, so a heading id never equals an item id); atlas-map, atlas-index, atlas-key-h, atlas-arrow, atlas-arrow-on
dom_hooks.namespace: atlas controls and boxes use atlas-* classes; the generic page classes link-btn, anchor, prose and section-intro are reused for a consistent look (none is reserved); no class of the foundation ATLAS_RESERVED_CLASSES appears; .term appears only as the page's glossary button (button.term[data-term]), whose card the interaction script shares with the mount; the renderer's formula boxes are renamed and the page's marks are not used
dom_hooks.words: interface words of the script travel as text in <template class='atlas-wordlist'> inside the mount (audited and font-subset with the page); no rule styles that class
dom_hooks.search_units: claims, domain cards, comparisons and paths are offered to the page search as [data-qh-unit][id] with a [data-qh-unit-title] heading; every claim also carries data-qh-unit-status, its page status by the ruling's aliases (checked, conditional, open, refuted form)

events_and_address.selection: the address: #atlas-c-<id>. Claim links, map marks, diagram marks, Follow and Previous/Next are ordinary in-page links; the browser makes the history entry; atlas.js follows hashchange and the page's qh:state. atlas.js never calls pushState/replaceState or assigns location
events_and_address.page anchors: a link inside the atlas to an id outside the mount is dispatched from the link as qh:navigate {id}; when the page handles it (preventDefault) the click's default is prevented, otherwise the browser follows the link
events_and_address.unknown claim address: not claimed (qh:unknown-anchor is not cancelled): the page shows its notice
events_and_address.keys: the atlas calls preventDefault for the keys it handles (index Up/Down/Home/End, Escape in the pane, Escape and Down in its filter field); Escape is left to the page while #card is shown
events_and_address.page search: a result inside the atlas: the page sets the address and dispatches qh:reveal; for a claim the atlas cancels it, shows the claim in the pane and focuses its heading; other atlas parts are left to the page
events_and_address.sheet: below 1000px a closed sheet stays closed until the address changes or the reader selects a claim; it closes when keyboard focus leaves it for the page

layout.no script and print: one column: key, map, domains, index, comparisons, paths, then every claim in full (#atlas-full)
layout.script, >= 1000px: #atlas-full is a sticky pane beside the atlas while it shows the selected claim, its diagram and its relation lists; with nothing selected the atlas has the full width
layout.script, < 1000px: #atlas-full becomes a sheet at the foot of the window while a claim is selected; Close and Escape hide it without changing the address
layout.print: pane, filters, diagram, path controls hidden; every claim, every index row (filter ignored), domains, comparisons and paths printed; #atlas starts a page
layout.order: key, then the map of every claim and relation, domains, index of claims, comparisons in the atlas, reading paths, every claim in full; each part opens with the question it answers
layout.proportion: one rhythm unit, the page's line (1.55 times the text on screen, 1.42 in print), and its quarter, half and one and a half for every space between blocks; headings at the page's weight 600 in sizes 1.3 / 1.16 / 1.08 by level; at 1000px and wider the atlas and the pane share the width 1.618 : 1; the map keeps its own size on screen (13px numbers; it scrolls in its box), a long domain runs over several columns of marks, and in print the map is fitted to the page reaching 13mm into each margin; an index of more than forty claims scrolls in its own box on screen with its head in view

design_choices_for_root: Glossary buttons (RC26, A3-RT-04): resolved by foundation, whose status.py no longer reserves the classes ctx.rich emits; atlas.py sets TERMS = True. An integration tree with an older foundation status.py that still reserves .term fails its build and names the class; then either update foundation or set TERMS = False (glossary definitions are then lost inside the atlas).

Placement and proportion at real scale (A3-RT-05): the atlas section comes after #status and before #results (foundation's order). At the 11:20 baseline's scale (503 claims) the atlas section is 3.5 MB of a 5.5 MB page without fonts and lists every claim in the index (in its own scroll box on screen) and in full (the pane on screen, every claim in print). Root decides whether the atlas follows the principal results and whether its claims in full print as an appendix.

Two 'Comparisons' (A2-RT-01): the page's nav 'Comparisons' goes to #frontier, 'The remaining comparisons' (foundation), and the atlas part is 'Comparisons in the atlas' (#atlas-comparisons); the atlas status word 'Remaining' is glossed 'Not settled: a comparison that remains to be made'. The content owner links an atlas comparison to its question on the page with comparisons[].questionId (shown as 'The question on this page:'), and decides whether the atlas's Remaining and the page's remaining comparisons are one vocabulary.

Status definitions (A2-RT-01, A2-IN-06): the key's four glosses use the contract's words; 'Conditional' is glossed as an implication with at least one hypothesis not established, to agree with the page key. The content owner confirms or replaces them (page.json atlas_gloss_<code>), and decides whether the atlas's statuses are the page's (one mark per word across the page) or a separate vocabulary (the present design: squares and an explicit key sentence).

Back after a row toggle: the page replaces the current history entry when a row opens, so Back cannot return to an atlas selection made before the toggle (observed in jsdom); the atlas may not keep state in history.state.
The tally 'Statements on this page' counts content.json statements only, not atlas claims.
Which relation codes are dependencies is not in the schema; until the content owner supplies it, a path is said to be joined by recorded relations.
statementRef links a claim to a statement of the page; showing that statement's own status beside the link needs a context capability (for example ctx.status_of(id)) from foundation.
A malformed atlas.json raises in foundation status.py (json.loads outside a try): a traceback instead of an audit failure.
The builder does not set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, so font subsets embed the build time; builds are reproducible only when the caller sets it.

asOf is read and never shown. A referee proposes 'As of <date>' in the atlas head when asOf differs from the page's date; the page's own date line is foundation's, and root decides whether the atlas states its own cut.

The 11:20 atlas is a review and layout baseline only. Its content findings (notation outside TeX read as identifiers or version tags; one question id the page does not have) are listed in LEDGER.md for the content owner; nothing of its text was edited.

Status labels (A4-RT-03): the 11:20 baseline gives each status several labels (for example Checked; Checked conclusion; Checked in stated scope; Checked within scope). The atlas shows each claim's own label in its card and in the index, and the filter reads it; whether the labels mark different standings is the content owner's to say (integration/completeness.py lists the variants as content findings).

Question links without the script (RD5): their static text is the interface phrase 'a question on this page'; the script puts in the question's heading. A foundation capability (for example ctx.title_of(anchor)) would let the server write the heading, for no-script reading and print.

Drafts (A4-IN-04): a draft (audit/rejected.html, or the page under --allow-draft) draws atlas text that fails the reader rules, as the page's own content does under --allow-draft. Root's draft policy decides whether such strings should be masked in drafts.
Atlas glossary terms are not described (A4-IN-07): the interaction script's description pass skips the mount, so an atlas .term[data-term] gets no aria-describedby. Owner: interaction.

The map shows claim numbers, not names (A3-RT-01, the principal's map rule V18: 'small labels beside their nodes, a readable key'): at real scale (503 claims) names beside every mark do not fit; names are given on hover, in the selected claim's pane and in the index beside the same numbers. A labelled map (larger, or labels for the selected claim and its relations) needs a page image to judge.
